messages.author: 9550825acfc56557
messages.subject: model averaging
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to model average multi-session models and I get two different error messages depending on which models I try to average:

I get this error when I try to average a D~session model and a model where Density is divided into 2 groups for the 5 sessions (D~ab):

Error in secr.lpredictor(formula = object1$model[[x]], newdata = newdata,  : 
  one or more model covariates not found in 'newdata'

I get this error when I try to average a 2 group and 3 group detection model (D~session g0~ab & D~session g0~abc)

Error in mat %*% beta[indx] : non-conformable arguments


Is there a way to average these models using secr? 

If not, does it make sense to average them by hand? 

Thanks for any insight!

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: model averaging
parts:
Hi Wes
This may be a tricky one to troubleshoot. I admit I am not especially excited about model averaging, so the code in 'secr' may be incomplete. My immediate suggestion is that you make sure to specify a 'newdata' argument with a column for each covariate referred to in the models, including 'session'. Factors should have the same levels as in the original data, and it doesn't matter if newdata includes irrelevant columns.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: model averaging
parts:
Wes

This function is buried inside 'secr'
se.untransform <- function (beta, sebeta, link) {
  switch (link,
          identity = sebeta,
          log = exp(beta) * sqrt(exp(sebeta^2)-1),
          neglog = exp(beta) * sqrt(exp(sebeta^2)-1),
          logit = invlogit(beta) * (1-invlogit(beta)) * sebeta,
          sin = NA)         ####!!!!
}

It's not exported, but after loading secr you can access it with e.g.,
secr:::se.untransform (5,2,'log')
[1] 1086.544

I must figure out the sin link some day...
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: model averaging
parts:
Hi Wes
The calculation in 'secr' takes into account sampling covariances among the beta s. You can see how it's done by peeking at another internal function:
secr:::secr.lpredictor
[some lines omitted]
        vcv <- beta.vcv[indx, indx, drop = FALSE]
        nrw <- nrow(mat)
        vcv <- apply(expand.grid(1:nrw, 1:nrw), 1, function(ij) mat[ij[1],
            , drop = F] %*% vcv %*% t(mat[ij[2], , drop = F]))
        vcv <- matrix(vcv, nrow = nrw)
        lpred[, 2] <- diag(vcv)^0.5
[more lines omitted]
Here 'indx' is a vector of indices for the beta parameters contributing to one real parameter. The final vcv is the variance covariance matrix of the transformed 'real' parameters - hence SEs are the sqrt of the diagonal. It's these SEs that are used in se.untransform.  Rows correspond to different rows of newdata (i.e. different covariate values, session etc.).

I suspect you don't really want to know! This sort of thing makes my head hurt, too, which is why I've been generally evasive about how to solve your actual problem. I know there are some good discussions of model averaging on the phidot MARK subforum (and also probably the Presence subforum) and I suggest you look there if you haven't already.
Murray
